infographic.title: How a Pressure Transmitter Works
infographic.alt: Infographic showing how a pressure transmitter works in four steps from diaphragm to 4 to 20 mA output
steps: Liquid, gas or steam pressure acts on a thin metal or ceramic diaphragm.
A strain gauge, capacitive cell or silicon chip turns the tiny diaphragm movement into an electrical change.
Electronics amplify the signal, compensate for temperature and linearize the output.
The transmitter sends 4 to 20 mA, HART or fieldbus data to the PLC or DCS.
